binders: An implicit profile f:Real->Real and implicit proposed derivative value f'.
Explicit real speed c, spatial coordinate x, and time t.
hypotheses: f has derivative f' at the characteristic foot x-c*t.
conclusions: For W(y,s)=f(y-c*s), W has temporal and spatial derivatives at (x,t) satisfying W_t+c*W_x=0.
The point x+c*t lies strictly to the right of x.
At time t the wave value at the displaced point is W(x+c*t,t)=f(x).
mathematical_definitions: The transport predicate includes existence of both one-variable partial derivatives with the other coordinate held fixed.
The value identity reduces algebraically to f((x+c*t)-c*t)=f(x).
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let c and t be positive. If a real profile f is differentiable at x-c t, then the traveling wave W(y,s)=f(y-c s) satisfies W_t+c W_x=0 at (x,t). Moreover x+c t>x, and the profile value initially labeled by x appears at the right-shifted point at time t: W(x+c t,t)=f(x).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The PDE conclusion is local at the single point (x,t); differentiability of f is assumed only at x-c*t.
The derivative value f' is universally bound but disappears from the conclusion; the assumption fixes it uniquely whenever it holds.
The propagation identity W(x+c*t,t)=f(x) is algebraic and does not require the differentiability hypothesis, though it is conjoined under that hypothesis.
Only positive c and positive t are covered; zero or negative speeds and nonpositive times are excluded.
No global claim that W solves the PDE at every point, no converse characterization of all PDE solutions, and no uniqueness, boundary condition, or norm estimate is encoded.
The PDE point (x,t) and the separately evaluated propagation point (x+c*t,t) are generally different.
